title: Eco‐friendly biostimulants enhance lettuce tolerance to drought stress in arid conditions by modulating phenolic compounds, anthocyanins and osmoprotectants
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

In arid Mediterranean regions frequent droughts threaten crops, demanding sustainable soil, water and plant management. This study aims to assess the influence of single and dual inoculation with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) on the growth, physiological performance and biochemical responses of lettuce cultivated in soils with or without compost amendment (C) under well-watered (WW; 100% crop evapotranspiration, ETc) and drought-stressed (DS; 50% ETc) regimes.

RESULTS

Total fresh weight (TFW), total dry weight (TDW), and yield (Y) of lettuce were reduced under DS, while C alone, or in combination with AMF or PGPR, improved TFW by 84%, 71% and 66%, respectively, compared to the control plants under DS. Y was highly significant in plants treated with C alone (84%) under DS compared to the control. It should be noted that the C-based treatments improved biochemical parameters, notably p-coumaric acid and kaempferol by C (79%) and AMF + C (18.37%), respectively, under DS compared to the control plants. Under the same conditions, C increased the anthocyanin content. In combination with PGPR, C was able to reduce hydrogen peroxide levels by 29% compared to the untreated plants. Proline and total soluble sugar content were significantly higher under DS. Mycorrhizal intensity reached 32%, particularly in plants inoculated with PGPR + AMF in C-amended soil under DS and improved post-harvest soil properties.

CONCLUSION

Consequently, compost alone or combined with rhizospheric microbes effectively enhanced yield, drought stress tolerance and soil–plant resilience. © 2025 Society of Chemical Industry.
